* *Programmatic support:* The highlight triggers during redirects (e.g., after a specific action that anchors the user back to a section).

fields.description:
h1. *Multiple Marking – Phase 3 updated 2026 Jun*

This document is an [+updated version of previous signed off requirements+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ko-PNO0BUlgYnFrZ8WU5RTC5JUAXhqCUSR1BKiJd7LY/edit?tab=t.0] by Monash team. The major updates are:

*Assignment level setting:*

* “Maximum total markers” → "Number of required markers" (This is covered in the [+meeting notes+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W_TsbgLLRpxgIXPLukzQlPBRQTER6-ANpfqF8R4JpyA/edit?tab=t.0])
* “Number of optional markers limit’ → "Number of optional markers" (This is covered in the [+meeting notes+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W_TsbgLLRpxgIXPLukzQlPBRQTER6-ANpfqF8R4JpyA/edit?tab=t.0])

*Site level setting terminology update:*

* “Maximum total markers limit” → “Maximum required markers limit” (This is confirmed in the [+MDL tracker+|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87709] comments by Michael)
* “Maximum number of optional markers limit” → “Maximum optional markers limit” (This is confirmed in the [+MDL tracker+|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87709] comments by Michael)

h1. Summary and Background:

Multiple Marking Phase 3 delivers two key enhancements that build on the functionality introduced in Phase 1 and Phase 2. These enhancements aim to improve marking governance, usability, and operational efficiency.

*Part 1: Basic Sample Marking*

This component enhances and extends the existing multiple marking framework introduced in Phase 1.

Key improvements include:

* Introduction of site-level marker settings to provide stronger governance and configuration control.
* Support for more detailed and flexible marking configurations.
* Improved consistency in the user experience when marking students.

This enhancement ensures a more scalable and controlled multiple marking model, reducing configuration ambiguity and improving marking reliability across units.

*Part 2: Filter Assignment Submissions by Grade*

This component enhances the Advanced Filter functionality on the View All Submissions page.

Key improvements include:

* Additional filtering capabilities based on grade values.
* Ability to sort students by grade.

These enhancements make the multiple marking feature more practical and efficient for coordinators and markers, particularly in large cohorts where grade analysis and targeted review are critical.

h2. *Part 3a - Basic Sample Marking*

These requirements define the configuration and behaviour of multiple markers in assignments using sample marking. They cover site-level and assignment-level settings, constraints on marker numbers, rules for increasing or reducing markers, grade calculation and recalculation, marker reassignment, and related UI behaviour. The intent is to ensure consistency, protect existing marking data, and provide clear, predictable outcomes for all students.

h2. 1. Configuration

1.1 Update the naming in the *assignment setting*:

* Update field name ‘Marker’ to ‘Number of required markers’
* Add a new field: ‘Number of optional markers’

*Site-level configuration*

h2. 1.2 *Maximum* required markers limit

The system should allow the site administrator to configure the maximum required markers limit at the site level. This value should be used as the maximum selectable value in the ‘Number of required markers’ dropdown in the assignment settings. When creating or editing an assignment, users must only be able to select marker values up to the configured site maximum.

* Any changes to the site-level maximum must be reflected immediately for newly created assignment configuration interfaces. 
* Any reduction to the site-level maximum setting should not impact existing assignments. All existing assignments should retain their current required marker without any changes.

h2. 1.3 *Maximum* optional markers limit

The system should allow the site administrator to define the maximum optional markers limit at the site configuration level. This value should be used as the upper limit for the *‘*Number of optional markers*’* dropdown within assignment settings. When creating or editing an assignment, users must only be able to select marker values up to the configured site maximum.

* Any changes to the site-level maximum must be reflected immediately for newly created assignment configuration interfaces. 
* Any reduction to the site-level maximum setting should not impact existing assignments. All existing assignments should retain their current optional marker settings without any changes.

h2. 1.4 *Default* number of required markers

The system should allow a site administrator to configure the ‘default number of required markers’ at the site level. The default required markers value should be less than or equal to the configured ‘maximum required markers limit’ value. This default value should be pre-selected in the number of required markers selection dropdown in the assignment settings.

h2. 1.5 *Default* number of optional markers

The system should allow a site administrator to configure the ‘default number of optional markers’ at the site level. The default optional markers value must be less than or equal to the configured ‘maximum optional markers limit’ value. This default value should be displayed and pre-selected in the number of optional markers selection dropdown in the assignment settings.

*Site Level Validation*

1.6 When a site administrator adjusts ‘maximum required markers limit’ or ‘maximum optional markers limit’, existing assignments must retain the existing selection values. The existing marker selection, marks and grades should be retained. When the updated value is saved, it will apply and display to newly created assignments. 

*Assignment Setting and Validation*

1.7 [+Number of required markers (Required markers)+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TfY2F8YXv_P4Wz1Q-BryMhwDUbnSY2yzkC-QvOmpaG8/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.nbrpy7yj5ok1] define the number of required markers that can be assigned to a student. 

1.8 [+Number of optional markers (Optional markers)+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TfY2F8YXv_P4Wz1Q-BryMhwDUbnSY2yzkC-QvOmpaG8/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.nbrpy7yj5ok1] defines the optional number of markers that can be assigned to a student. 

1.9 In the assignment settings, the number of required marker selection dropdowns must not allow a value of 0. The minimum selectable value must be greater than 0.

1.11 Number of required markers, Number of optional markers, increasing or decreasing required or optional markers applies to all students in the unit.

----

h2. 2. Marker Numbers and Grade Calculation

2.1 The system should calculate and display a grade (in the grade column) when:

* If required markers are allocated and no optional markers are enabled, all required markers have marked and marking workflow status is set to marking completed. 
* If one or more required markers have not entered a mark (marking status is not _marking completed_), the system must not calculate or display a grade.

*OR*

* If required markers + optional markers enabled, all required markers and all enabled optional markers have marked and marking workflow status is set to Marking completed.
* Optional markers that are not enabled (unchecked checkboxes) must be ignored for grade calculation.

2.2 When grade has been calculated. If an optional marker is enabled (e.g., checkbox ticked), existing markers mark and feedback should be retained, if the grade already exists display a pop up asking for a confirmation that grades will be cleared/reset to null/empty. When an optional marker has been assigned and marked, the system will calculate the grade.

2.3 In the assignment setting, changing the calculation method (e.g., from average to maximum) is allowed at any time, even post mark release, it requires user confirmation (e.g., popup: "This will update agreed grades for all students. Yes?"). If the user selects yes, It triggers grade recalculation for all affected students. If user select no, the calculation method remain unchanged

----

h2. 3. Increasing Marker Numbers

3.1 Increasing the required/optional markers should be applied to all students in the assignment. The system evaluates each student individually, and the configuration change applies to all the students within the assignment.

3.2 In assignment setting, increasing the required markers is allowed at any time. All the markers’ marks, feedback and grades are retained. When the required markers are increased, the number of optional markers must remain unchanged.

Example: Required marker is 2 and optional marker is 2, increasing required marker from 2 to 3

* When Marker 3 and 4 have not been assigned/marked, the system will increase the required marker to 3, optional markers will shift to marker 4 and marker 5.
* When Marker 3 and 4 have been assigned/marked, the system will increase the required marker to 3, marker 3 and 4 will shift to marker 4 and marker 5. Optional markers’ marks, feedback and grades are retained.

3.3 In assignment setting, increasing the optional markers is allowed at any time. All the markers’ marks, feedback and grades are retained. When the optional markers are increased, the number of required markers must remain unchanged.

Example: Required marker is 2 and optional marker is 2, increasing optional marker from 2 to 3

* When Marker 3 and 4 have not been assigned/marked, the system will increase the optional marker to 3, the newly added optional markers will be marker 5.
* When Marker 3 and 4 have been assigned/marked, the system will increase the optional marker to 3, the newly added optional markers will be marker 5. Marker 3 and 4s’ marks, feedback and grades are retained.

----

h2. 4. Reducing Marker Numbers

4.1 Reducing the required/optional number of markers, this should be applied to all students in the assignment. The system evaluates each student individually, and the configuration change applies to all the students within the assignment.

4.2 In assignment setting, reducing the required markers are allowed when:

* The marker being removed has not been assigned to the student.

Example: Required marker is 5 and optional marker is 0, 

* If Marker 5 has been not been assigned to any student, the total number of markers can be reduced to 4 (removing Marker 5). 
* If Marker 5 has been assigned to any student, the total number of markers cannot be reduced.

4.3 In assignment setting, reducing optional number of markers is allowed when:

* The marker being removed has not been assigned to or enabled for any student.

Example: If the required marker is 2 and the optional marker is 2, marker 4 has been enabled and allocated to one student, for other students marker 4 is not enabled, in the assignment setting the optional number of markers cannot be reduced.

Example: Required marker is 4 and optional marker is 1, reducing optional marker from 1 to 0

* When Marker 5 has not been assigned or enabled to any student, the number of optional markers can be reduced to 0. 
* When Marker 5 has been enabled but not assigned, the number of optional markers limit can not be reduced to 0. 
* When Marker 5 is assigned, the number of optional markers limit can not be reduced to 0.

----

h2. 5. Reassign Marker

5.1 Reassigning a marker is only permitted when the assigned marker’s marking status is ‘Not marked’. Once the marker has marked, or the marking status is anything other than ‘Not marked’, it cannot be reassigned to another marker.

----

h2. 6. UI Rules for total marker, minimum marker, optional marker slots

6.1 The required markers allocation slots show with no checkbox. (Refer to UI example 1)

fields.description:
We have done our discovery work on adding react into core. This issue is for reviewing the code on [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|smart-link] and make sure that it adheres to Moodle coding guidelines, makes improvements where possible, and does not cause any regressions
One of the completion criteria is ensuring that developer documentation is provide. 

When working through this issue, please consider:

* Identify code that is no longer needed
* Remove any experimental scaffolding
* Simplify any code that we put in to produce a working result
* Challenge if each part is needed
* Reduce complexity if possible

*Merge plan*

This issue introduces Esbuild as the build system for React code in Moodle. The primary architectural decision is the introduction of a dedicated {{js/react/}} directory, keeping React logic physically and logically separate from legacy AMD code.

*Dedicated Source Organisation*

React source files are located in {{js/react/src/}} rather than {{amd/src/}} because they are native ES modules and are not processed through Moodle’s AMD pipeline.

* *Location:* {{[plugin]/js/react/src/ }}(additional subdirectories may be defined beneath src/ as needed)
* This separation clearly distinguishes React-based code from AMD modules and prevents existing Grunt/Shifter tasks from attempting to process files they do not support.

*Output Format and Build Integration*

While the code lives in a new folder, *Esbuild* is configured to output the transpiled results in a way that our existing systems can still understand.

* *Multiple Entry Points:* Esbuild maps each file in {{js/react/src/}} to a corresponding output in {{js/react/build/}}.
* *Format Consistency:* We utilize Esbuild's flexibility to ensure the output remains compatible with Moodle's page requirements manager, even though it lives outside the traditional {{amd/}} folder.
* *Zero Config Discovery:* The build script automatically scans all {{js/react/}} directories across the entire Moodle tree. The discovery occurs at build time and does not affect runtime performance.

*Benefits of the js/react/ separation*

* *Gradual transition:* Features can transition from AMD / YUI to React without restructuring existing modules
* *Linting & Tooling:* We can apply stricter TypeScript and React-specific linting rules (MDL-87988) to the {{js/react/}} folder without triggering thousands of "legacy" errors in the old {{amd/}} code.

*Centralised Bundling:* By centralising React code here, Esbuild can more efficiently handle *Tree Shaking* and *Dynamic Imports*, ensuring that we don't duplicate the React runtime across different plugins.

This is one of two blockers to using the new certification tooling at build.1edtech to certify (or re-certify) our LTI Provider as LTI Advantage Complete. Right now, during a deep linking workflow, after content selection (and assuming “add to gradebook” IS checked), the cert. suite reports:

{noformat}"errors": [
    "'label' should be a string",
    "'tag' should be a string"
],{noformat}

Moodle doesn’t set label or tag on the lineitem when returning it as part of the content item, however. See the code responsible for that response here:
[https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/f747c15cbf1c1c963a9592a73b167b969ec33d75/public/enrol/lti/configure.php#L76|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/f747c15cbf1c1c963a9592a73b167b969ec33d75/public/enrol/lti/configure.php#L76|smart-link] 

What should happen is that, because we’ve omitted those fields (i.e. we’re not calling setLabel() or setTag()), the label and tag properties should be excluded from the contentitem’s lineitem. These fields are optional per the spec: [https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-dl/v2p0#lti-resource-link|https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-dl/v2p0#lti-resource-link|smart-link]  

If these fields are omitted, the certification suite’s diagnosis window reports everything is green and passing.

I’ve reported this bug upstream([https://github.com/packbackbooks/lti-1-3-php-library/issues/169|https://github.com/packbackbooks/lti-1-3-php-library/issues/169|smart-link] ), but even when that lands and we upgrade our library, it won’t fix the issue in stables. We need to patch that locally if we want to use the new certification site for the re-certification of stable+sec versions - and we do, since it saves ~90 mins per Moodle version being certified + is more accurate, which is win-win for us.

fields.summary: Minor change in curl class breaks Microsoft O365 plugin

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
We have identified that the change to the {{PUT}} method signature in the {{curl}} class — introduced in the following commit: [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/commit/161837e393b84ce43525eb88250689bc059b3f0a|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/commit/161837e393b84ce43525eb88250689bc059b3f0a|smart-link] has broken compatibility with the Microsoft O365 plugin. This caused a 500 error across all our platforms, preventing users from authenticating via OIDC : 


{noformat}PHP Fatal error:  Declaration of local_o365\httpclient::put($url, $params = [], $options = []): string|bool must be compatible with curl::put($url, $params = [], $options = [], $includeuserpwd = true) in /var/www/html/local/o365/classes/httpclient.php on line 160{noformat}

A straightforward merge request has been submitted to Microsoft: [https://github.com/microsoft/o365-moodle/pull/3019|https://github.com/microsoft/o365-moodle/pull/3019|smart-link] 

However, I am questioning whether it is standard practice for such a breaking change to occur within a minor update of version 5.0. Perhaps this is not an intended change, which is why I’m reporting it here.

fields.summary: New page surfaces and activity card states

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

fields.description:
h3. Design rationale

Activity cards have no fill and no border, so they don't react to the pointer or the keyboard.

A section body can hold twenty activities. With no edge between them they read as one undifferentiated list, and you have to use the text to work out where one activity stops and the next begins. Giving each card a border makes the section scannable at a glance.

Hover fills the card white so you can see which one the pointer is on as you move down a long section. Focus goes back to grey with a blue ring instead, so keyboard position never gets confused with mouse position: two different questions, two different answers.

The subsection chevron is currently smaller than the section chevron. That implies subsections are a lesser kind of thing, which isn't true — they're a peer structure, and should look like one.

h3. What needs changing

*Activity card states*

||State||Fill||Border||
|Rest|{{$mds-bg-surface-subtle}} {{#f8f9fa}}|1px {{$mds-border-default}} {{#dee2e6}}|
|Hover|{{$mds-bg-surface-default}} {{#ffffff}}|unchanged|
|Focus|back to {{#f8f9fa}}|{{$mds-border-interactive-primary-default}} {{#0f6cbf}} + ring|
|Hover + focus|{{#ffffff}}|as focus|

* The fill at rest is the same grey as the body behind it, so the border is the card's only edge.
* Focus must not change the card's size — outline and shadow, not border width.
* Same behaviour inside a section and inside a subsection. A subsection renders _inside_ an activity card so exclude it or the whole subsection lights up. Only the edit-mode outline is guarded today.
* Hidden activities keep their distinct look and a visible edge.
* -Edit mode keeps its existing blue hover outline, unchanged.-

*Section header line*

* Match the subsection chevron to the section chevron: 32×32 with a 16px glyph, not 24×24/14px.
* Centre the chevron, title, badges, action menu and collapse-all on the header line. 

+Presentation only. No behaviour change.+

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Open question*

Divider colour. MDL-87805 shipped the header/body divider as #e9ecef (border/subtle); Figma uses #dee2e6 (border/default). Which is right, and does the fix belong here or in a follow-up to MDL-87805?
{panel}

h3. How to test

# Course page, not editing — every activity card is grey with a visible border against the grey section body.
# Point at a card — it fills white, the border doesn't change, nothing shifts.
# Tab to a card — grey fill returns, blue border and ring appear, the card doesn't resize and the page doesn't reflow.
# Point at the card you've tabbed to — it stays white.
# Point inside a subsection — only the activity under the pointer changes, not the subsection.
# Hidden activity still reads as hidden and still has an edge.
# -Turn editing on — the blue hover outline behaves as it did before.-
# Section and subsection chevrons are the same size; both header lines are centred.

h3. Design

Figma — [https://www.figma.com/design/rlo17bSNmm9tChVnLgbJa6/MDL-87755---LMS-uplift--phase-1-?node-id=4501-45992&m=dev|https://www.figma.com/design/rlo17bSNmm9tChVnLgbJa6/MDL-87755---LMS-uplift--phase-1-?node-id=4501-45992&m=dev|smart-link]

fields.summary: Restyle activity dates as badges

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

fields.description:
Rescoped. The design has moved on since this ticket was written. Dates use one neutral badge treatment for every type, not colour-coded tags — see the first bullet under Expected behaviour.

h2. Proposed change

Restyle activity dates as badges, and align the dates row with the card's left edge.

Dates currently render as plain text rows. The badge is a small bordered pill with the label and date on one line.

The dates row sits flush with the card's left padding edge, aligned with the title rather than indented to the title text. Two dates sit side by side on one row and wrap together rather than stacking.

No calendar icon, and one treatment for every date type.

h2. User goal

Read an activity's dates as discrete, scannable facts rather than a run of grey text under the description.

h2. Preconditions

* "Show activity dates" is on for the course; test again with it off.
* Test course contains activities covering every shape in the table below, plus one with no dates set.
* Test course has activities inside a subsection as well as directly in a section.
* Contrast is measured against the new fills from [MDL-87833|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87833].

h2. Expected behaviour

On colour: this ticket originally asked for coloured tags with a consistent colour per date type. That is reversed — all date types share one neutral badge. Besides matching the current design, it removes an accessibility problem, since colour-coded date types would need a non-colour carrier as well. The tense of a date is already carried by its label.

The badge has to hold seven date shapes:

||Shape||Example||
|One date|Forum with a due date|
|Two, both past|Choice that has opened and closed|
|Two, both future|Database that has not opened yet|
|Two, mixed tense|Lesson open now and closing later — proof that tense is per date, not per activity|
|Module-specific pair|Assignment, where a submission deadline is not the same as the activity closing|
|Close with no open|Quiz with only a close date set|
|Four dates|Workshop, which contributes the most of any module. They render flat, each carrying its own phase in the label|

* The badge's height is the outer box including its border.
* The label and the date are visibly separated — the gap must be explicit, not inherited from the markup.
* Labels use the existing core date strings. No new strings, no new date sources.
* The label stays programmatically tied to its date, so a screen reader reads "Closes: Monday 26 February" as one phrase.
* Text meets contrast on the grey activity card and on a white subsection header.
* The badge's border is decorative — the badge is understandable without it.
* Test text-spacing overrides explicitly. A fixed badge height is exactly what that breaks.
* At high zoom the row wraps; nothing truncates, clips, or causes the page to scroll sideways.
* No new interactive elements, so no new keyboard or focus requirements.

h2. Test cases

* Each of the seven shapes renders with the right label and tense, including one past and one future badge together on the mixed-tense case.
* Activity with no dates: nothing rendered, no empty container or stray spacing.
* Badge height matches Figma including the border, with a visible gap between label and date.
* Dates row aligns with the card's left padding edge; two dates sit side by side and wrap together.
* "Show activity dates" off: no dates anywhere.
* Text meets contrast on the grey card and inside a subsection.
* High zoom and increased text spacing: wraps, nothing clipped, no sideways page scroll.
* Screen reader reads label and date as one phrase.
* Workshop: all four badges render on one wrapping row, each keeping its own phase label.

h2. Release coordination

Contrast is measured against the fills [MDL-87833|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87833] introduces, so the two release together. Shares spacing with [MDL-89324|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89324] (restriction box), which sits directly below the dates row.

Out of scope: the Figma also shows workshop's four dates wrapped in named groups with the phase prefix dropped from the badges inside. That is not in this ticket. Core's dates API has no grouping concept, so it would need either a new capability there or workshop-specific handling in shared rendering code. Workshop's dates render flat here.

fields.description:
React will be treated as a platform provided dependency. In this issue we are downloading the relevant react files (react, react-dom/client, jsx-runtime, jsx-dev-runtime) from [https://esm.sh|https://esm.sh]
Ensure that the importmap is updated to point to the locations of these files. Use the code on [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|smart-link] to determine the location. The readme needs to provide full details of how to update the files. Also make sure to add a record in the thirdpartylibs.xml file. This lists all of the third party libraries included in core and their licence.

*Merge Plan*

This issue focuses on the controlled acquisition and serving of the React library. React source files are not exposed as public web assets. They are protected resources served exclusively through the Moodle routing layer.

Instead of placing React files in a publicly accessible folder like {{/lib/javascript.php}}, we will store the "vendored" ESM files in a directory *outside the public web root.*

* *Security:* This prevents direct access to library files outside of the routing layer.
* *Integrity:* Only the Moodle routing system has the permissions to read from this location and serve the content.

Because the files aren't in a public folder, the browser can't "see" them via a standard URL. The router acts as the bridge:

# *Request:* The browser asks for {{react}} via the Import Map.
# *Resolution:* The router maps that request to the internal, non-public file path.
# *Streaming:* The router reads the file and returns it with the appropriate MIME type and cache headers.

This issue includes the tool used to maintain these protected files.

* *Source:* Uses *esm.sh* to pull React and React-DOM in a clean, bundled ESM format. The downloaded files are committed to the repository and are not fetched dynamically at runtime
* *Local Vendoring:* The script downloads the specific, pinned version into the protected internal directory.
* *Verification:* The script can be expanded to verify the integrity of the downloaded files, ensuring the core library hasn't been tampered with.

fields.description:
h2. What is this issue?

This improvement intends to include all possible third-party libraries using Composer.

Initially this will co-exist with the current approach and we will have them *at the same version as* the versions in Moodle core while we get people used to updating and installing from Composer.

We will also:

* be keeping those dependencies in Moodle until Moodle 6.0.
* only be including those dependencies which have no modifications.
* have to add something to ensure that the {{autoload.files}} are only included if the non-composer version has not already been included (only impacts AWS/SDK).

h2. Why is this important?

This is, essentially, a blocker to the Open Telemetry work because that work will require that some Open Telemetry packages be installed. Some of those Open Telemetry packages will then pull in other dependencies, such as a PSR7 handler, some PSR packages, and more. We already have several of those things and we want to be careful that we don’t end up with _different_ versions included. We want a single source of truth.

h2. Tell me more about versions

Initially we need to make sure that all package versions match the currently installed versions.

When we properly mandate the use of Composer in 6.0, this will need to block the upgrade and installation of Moodle because we have dependencies on things like Mustache.

If we bump any versions of any dependencies we will need to keep them in-sync.

h2. Other things

There are a _couple_ of libraries with local Moodle modifications. For now, we are *_not_* going to include them until we determine the best approach going forward.

We _could_ decide to only do this for the dependencies that we think we are _likely_ to use… but we just don’t know what the limits are there and it seems like a bad idea to me!

The list of modified libraries is currently:

* phpspreadsheet
* xhprof
* php-css-parser (needs major version upgrade)
* google SDK
* scss-php (needs major version upgrade)
* tcpdf

We also exclude our own RTLCSS library because it is heavily dependant upon php-css-parser.

fields.summary: Wrong version bumping from MDL-83985

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
[https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|smart-link] introduces wrong version bumpings.

The patch was introduced/rebased shortly after the Moodle 5.0 release to the {{main}} branch of the day. That branch is now the 5.1 branch.

Just before the 5.0 release we perform a version bump for all plugins which increases the version number to the release date, that is {{2025041400}}.

When applying upgrade steps to the {{main}} branch we must always use the current date and this must also be a few days later than the previous release date.

Unforuntately [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|smart-link] did not follow the documented procedures and used a microbump to {{2025041401}} - this fits into the reserved version numberign for the 5.0.x release series. They should have used the “today’s date” of the day, which woudl have beens something like {{2025052200}}

As a result, any change to a plugin on 5.0 which increases the version to a number higher than {{2025041401}} will break all of thse upgrade steps on 5.1 and main. Essentially if we bump the version for any activity plugin on 5.0.x, anyone upgrading from at least that 5.0.x release will not get the 5.1 version bump.

The best fix here is to:

* bump the version.php for all impacted plugins to the _new_ 5.1 release microbump (most of them are {{2025100600}} and will become {{2025100601}}.
* update the {{public/mod/[name]/upgrade.php}} for each to:
** move the step introduced in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|smart-link] to the end fo the function (just before the {{return true;}})
** change the version number in that diffset to the new one we just bumped

We can probably skip this on the {{main}} branch beacuse we haven’t actually bumped any of these plugin’s version numbers _yet_ (I don’t think). If we have then we will need to *copy this step* and bump to *today’s date* but only forthe impacted plugins.

* provide a consistent developer experience for React components
